entities.summary:
The Independent Greeks (Ανεξάρτητοι Έλληνες) is a nationalist political party founded in Greece in 2012 amidst the severe socioeconomic crisis that gripped the nation. Headquartered on Andrea Syngrou Avenue in Athens, this party emerged as a response to the public's growing discontent with mainstream parties perceived as responsible for austerity measures imposed by international creditors. Led by Panos Kammenos, a former member of the New Democracy party, it appealed to voters by emphasizing national sovereignty, anti-austerity sentiments, and a staunch opposition to illegal immigration, thus playing a pivotal role in reshaping the political landscape of Greece during the 2010s.

Following its establishment, the Independent Greeks capitalized on the rising tide of populism in Europe, securing 7.5% of the vote in the 2012 parliamentary elections, which translated to 33 seats in the Hellenic Parliament. Their participation in the government formed by the left-wing SYRIZA party after the January 2015 elections marked a significant moment in Greek politics, as it highlighted the uneasy alliance between radical left and right-wing factions against austerity measures imposed by the EU and the IMF. They held the position of junior coalition partner, significantly influencing policies and public discourse surrounding national identity and economic recovery.
